title: Low-bit batching: regional SLA sensitivity notes
summary: Working spreadsheet-style notes exploring tradeoffs between low-bit (3/4-bit) quantization and dynamic batching across regions and GPU types. Focus is on meeting 95th-percentile latency SLAs while maximizing throughput and minimizing token cost. Includes sensitivity slices for cache hit-rate, KV-prefetch, and burst windows.
assumptions: FP16 baseline measured on H100: 120 req/s per card at 8k prompt mix (median request = 240 tokens)
4-bit QAT/LLM-int8-equivalent profile gives ~1.9x throughput vs FP16; 3-bit yields ~2.6x but larger quality delta
Cache hit-rate modeled as prefix KV cache: 0%/50%/80% scenarios tested
Batching uses dynamic window up to max_batch_size; added tail latency from waiting is modeled as 1.2x latency cost per 50ms batching window
Regions: us-west (H100-heavy), eu-central (mixed H100+A100), ap-southeast (A100 spot-heavy)
Cost per token estimated from reserved GPU unit economics and average packing: approximate and intended for relative comparison only

sensitivity_scenarios: KV cache hit 0%: 3-bit configs regularly miss 95th latency SLA in all regions; 4-bit sometimes misses on mixed fleets
KV cache hit 50%: us-west 3-bit improves 95th from 125ms -> 95ms (meets SLA), eu-central still borderline; effective throughput increases ~1.2x for cache-backed requests
KV cache hit 80%: 4-bit becomes safe operating point across most regions; token cost reduces further as cache avoids recompute for prefixes
Dynamic batching window 0ms (no waiting): throughput drops by expected batching factor (~batch size ratio), 95th latency improves but throughput loss may raise unit cost
Burst policy (allow overflow to Dedicated pool): keeps SLA for 3-bit at high QPS but requires reserved headroom (20-30% capacity reserve)
cost_model_notes: TokenCost_per_1k is approximate relative unit: baseline FP16=1.00 in us-west. Secondary regions account for spot discounts and lower packing.
Low-bit profiles reduce GPU time per token but increase risk of output-quality regression; cost savings should be weighted by eval pass/fail rate for key prompt sets
Operational overhead: 3-bit requires more conservative rollout, stronger evaluation gating, and automatic fallback to 4-bit/FP16 on quality regressions
recommended_operating_points: us-west: prefer 4-bit with batch sizes 12-16 + prefix cache >=50% for latency-sensitive routes. Use 3-bit only for best-effort / background inference with fallback.
eu-central: run conservative 4-bit in mixed fleet; invest in kernel optimizations for A100 to close latency gap before 3-bit rollout.
ap-southeast: treat as cost-optimized region — use 4-bit for non-latency-critical workloads; keep FP16 for latency SLOs when spot volatility high.

raw_notes: Quick findings: low-bit materially improves throughput and lowers cost-per-token, but 3-bit pushes 95th latency and quality risk without high cache-hit rates and conservative batching. For production latency SLOs, 4-bit + prefix cache looks like the best medium-term balance. Need more A/B evals on customer prompt sets to quantify quality deltas beyond perplexity (F1/QA accuracy for retrieval-augmented routes).
